newsitem.title: FRANCE: DHL works on contingency strike plans.
newsitem.headline: DHL works on contingency strike plans.

text.p: DHL Worldwide Express said it was working on contingency plans in anticipation of a one-day strike on October 17 by French public sector workers which is being supported by air traffic controllers.
The French civil aviation authority, the DGAC, said flights to and from French airports will be reduced to around 15 percent of normal from 0500 GMT on October 17 to 0500 GMT, October 18.
Surveillance of aircraft overflying French airspace will be normal, the DGAC added.

DHL operates scheduled overnight all-cargo services between its Brussels hub and French provincial airports in Bordeaux, Lyon, Marseille, Mulhouse, Nice and Toulouse with a mixture of Electra and Convair aircraft.
The express distribution group also operates a Bergamo-Paris/CDG and East Midlands airport rotation with a Boeing 727F.

"Additional trucking services to and from Brussels will probably be the main pillar of our makeshift operation but, where possible, we'll consider using alternative airports, for example, Geneva in place of Lyon, Basle as a substitute for Mulhouse and Vittoria in northern Spain, as a temporary hub for Toulouse and Bordeaux traffic, Yves Cortet, DHL France line-haul operations manager, told Reuters.

"While at this moment in time we can't say to what degree our flight network will be affected, we don't want to run the risk of our aircraft landing at French airports and then finding they are grounded because clearance to leave can't be granted," he added.
DHL will also consider delaying its flight from Brussels to Nantes for several hours until after the 0500 GMT expiry of the strike on October 18, Cortet added.
